findings.description: Critical: wp-skills' verification gate is unsatisfiable within its own write scope. Task 3.6 (wp-skills) closes `openspec/schemas/provider-model-map.schema.json` to the five-key roster via `propertyNames.enum` + `required`, but `skills/tests/vendor-neutral-autopilot/test_contracts.py:88` (`test_default_provider_model_map_conforms_to_stable_schema`) validates the LIVE `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.DEFAULT_PROVIDER_MODEL_MAP` (imported at test_contracts.py:8) against that schema. That map is edited by task 2.3, which lives in wp-coordinator. wp-skills declares `depends_on: [wp-empirical]` only (work-packages.yaml:180) and runs in an ISOLATED worktree (`mode: isolated`, line 210), so wp-coordinator's edits are not present; `agent-coordinator/**` is also absent from wp-skills' `write_allow` (lines 194-200), so the agent cannot fix it. VERIFIED by simulating task 3.6's tightening against the current map: 4 validation errors -- "'antigravity' is a required property", "'grok' is a required property", "'pi' is a required property", "'gemini' is not one of ['claude_code','codex','antigravity','grok','pi']". The same cross-tree coupling hits task 3.1: `skills/tests/vendor-neutral-autopilot/test_model_resolution.py:50,53,62,73,75,125,127,169,173` asserts directly against `DEFAULT_PROVIDER_MODEL_MAP["providers"][...]`, so rewriting it to the new roster yields KeyError in wp-skills' worktree. wp-skills' gate command (line 220) runs `pytest skills/tests`, which collects both files. Result: wp-skills can never go green, and neither can wp-docs-finalize, which depends on it.
findings.resolution: Add `wp-coordinator` to wp-skills' `depends_on` (they already have disjoint write scopes, so serializing costs only wall-clock), OR move task 3.6 and the `skills/tests/vendor-neutral-autopilot/` roster edits into wp-coordinator so the schema closure and the map it validates land in one worktree. The first is smaller and preserves D8.1's tree-ownership boundary.

findings.description: Critical: wp-frontend's gate cannot pass in the isolated worktree it declares. The gate's first clause is `(cd apps/kanban-viz && npm test -- --run)` (work-packages.yaml:278) and the package sets `worktree.mode: isolated` (line 268). `apps/kanban-viz/node_modules` is gitignored and per-checkout, and `skills/worktree/scripts/worktree-bootstrap.sh` provisions only the two Python venvs (`uv sync --all-extras` at lines 41 and 47) -- it never runs `npm ci`/`npm install`, and `git grep -n 'node_modules|npm ci|npm install'` over the worktree scripts, tasks.md and work-packages.yaml returns nothing. VERIFIED empirically in this very worktree: `cd apps/kanban-viz && npm test -- --run` -> `sh: vitest: command not found`; `ls -d node_modules` -> No such file or directory (the shared checkout at /Users/jankneumann/Coding/agentic-coding-tools/apps/kanban-viz/node_modules does have it, which is why this was invisible during planning). The same clause terminates wp-docs-finalize's step-2 `&&` chain (line 365) and task 4.3's checkpoint.
findings.resolution: Add an `npm ci --prefix apps/kanban-viz` step to Phase 0 (it is exactly the baseline-repair class D8.4 quarantines) and prepend it to the wp-frontend and wp-docs-finalize gate commands, or extend `worktree-bootstrap.sh` to install JS deps when `apps/kanban-viz/package.json` is present.

findings.description: Critical: D7's baseline-repair table enumerates three pre-existing broken gates but misses a fourth, and it is the first clause of wp-coordinator's gate. VERIFIED on this branch, unmodified: `agent-coordinator/.venv/bin/python -m pytest agent-coordinator/tests -q -m 'not e2e and not integration'` -> `3 failed, 2027 passed, 1 skipped, 90 deselected`. The failures are `test_docker_manager.py::TestDetectRuntime::test_auto_falls_back_to_podman` (`assert 'docker' == 'podman'`), `TestStartContainer::test_successful_start` (unexpected `colima_started: True` key), and `TestStartContainer::test_compose_up_fails`. `git log --oneline main..HEAD -- agent-coordinator/tests/test_docker_manager.py agent-coordinator/src/docker_manager.py` is empty, so this is pre-existing and host-environment-dependent (a real docker + podman + colima are on this machine and leak past the mocks; CI's ubuntu runner likely passes). Because wp-coordinator's verification (work-packages.yaml:144) and wp-docs-finalize's step 2 (line 365) are `&&` chains beginning with this suite, and both run `cwd: "."` on the operator's machine, neither package can report green.
findings.resolution: Add a Phase 0 task alongside 0.1: either repair the three `test_docker_manager.py` mocks so they are host-independent, or add an explicit deselection (`--deselect agent-coordinator/tests/test_docker_manager.py::...`) to the two gate commands with the reason recorded in D7's table. Silently leaving it makes the gate a known-red check, which is the vacuous-gate failure mode D8.2 exists to remove.

findings.description: Critical: the mirror-residue check in task 6.1 and in wp-docs-finalize's step 2 (work-packages.yaml:365) is vacuous -- it passes today, before any work, and would pass even if `install.sh` were never run. `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are gitignored (`.gitignore:271` and `:272`) and therefore untracked; `git ls-files .claude/skills` and `git ls-files .agents/skills` both return nothing. `git grep` searches tracked files only -- which is precisely the property design.md § Scope inventory relies on for the other gates, and precisely what makes it meaningless here. VERIFIED: `git grep -lIi gemini -- .claude/skills .agents/skills ':!*SKILL.md' ':!*/references/*' ':!*/templates/*' ':!*/install_assets/*'` returns 0 files right now, while the same search on disk (`grep -rlI -i gemini`) returns 32 files, including `.claude/skills/collect-transcripts/scripts/adapters/gemini_cli.py`, `.claude/skills/autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py` and `.agents/skills/langfuse/scripts/install-mcp.sh`. This is a second-order instance of the exact defect D8.2 was written to eliminate. (The sync itself is fine: `skills/install.sh:692` uses `rsync -a --checksum --delete`, so the deleted adapter really would be removed -- only the verification is empty.)
findings.resolution: Replace `git grep` with a working-tree search for the two untracked mirror trees, e.g. `! grep -rlI -i gemini .claude/skills .agents/skills --exclude='SKILL.md' --exclude-dir=references --exclude-dir=templates --exclude-dir=install_assets --exclude-dir=__pycache__ | grep .`, in both task 6.1 and the wp-docs-finalize step-2 chain. Note the design's "gates must use git grep, never bare grep -r" rule is correct for tracked trees and inapplicable here; record that exception.

findings.description: Critical: five of the nine test locations task 3.1 is required to rewrite are executed by no gate in this plan and by no CI job, so the roster assertions written there are unverifiable. Task 3.1 lists `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/`, `skills/parallel-infrastructure/tests/test_vendor_diversity.py` and `skills/autopilot/scripts/tests/test_implementation_strategy_selector.py`, but every pytest invocation in the plan is either `pytest skills/tests`, `pytest agent-coordinator/tests`, `pytest packages/agent-scenarios/tests`, or `npm test` -- none of those paths is under `skills/tests`. CI does not cover them either: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:64` runs `uv run pytest -v` from `skills/`, which uses `skills/pyproject.toml` `testpaths` (lines 46-83) -- that list omits `parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests`, `parallel-infrastructure/tests` and `autopilot/scripts/tests`. (`skills/fix-scrub/tests/test_vendor_dispatch.py` is the one exception -- ci.yml:83 runs it.) Worse, those files cannot currently be collected at all: `skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/test_review_dispatcher.py skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/test_consensus_synthesizer.py ...` -> `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'consensus_synthesizer'`, and there is no conftest.py in that tree. A "write failing tests" instruction against a directory whose tests never run is indistinguishable from writing nothing.
findings.resolution: Either add those paths to the wp-skills gate command explicitly (with whatever sys.path fix they need -- a conftest.py mirroring `skills/tests/vendor-neutral-autopilot/conftest.py` would do it), or drop them from task 3.1 and record in design.md that their gemini references are deferred with the D6 narrative set. Do not leave them listed as edited-but-unverified.

findings.description: Nit: task 4.2 is printed under "Phase 4 -- Kanban frontend" and declares `Dependencies: 2.7, 0.1`, but work-packages.yaml:177 assigns it to wp-skills, whose `depends_on` is `[wp-empirical]`. Task 2.7 lives in wp-coordinator. The package DAG therefore does not encode task 4.2's stated dependency, and the work-packages validator does not catch it (`validate_work_packages.py` -> VALID: schema/depends_on_refs/dag_cycles/lock_keys all pass -- it checks package-level edges only). `skills/tests/agent-coordinator/test_kanban_viz_endpoints.py` is one of 16 files under `skills/tests` that reach into the coordinator tree, so this is the same class as finding 1 rather than an independent hazard.
findings.resolution: Covered by finding 1's resolution (wp-skills depends_on wp-coordinator). If that is rejected, renumber task 4.2 into Phase 3 and drop the 2.7 dependency, since the five-vendor fixture is derivable from `contracts/roster.md` without the seeder change.

findings.description: Nit: `docs/cross-repo-setup.md` meets D6's own inclusion criterion -- "anything that instructs a human or a script to invoke gemini" -- but is absent from the in-scope doc set (design.md § In-scope user-facing set), from task 5.3, and from every gate. Line 348 states install-mcp.sh "registers the Langfuse MCP server with Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini (`~/.gemini/settings.json`) in one shot", and line 384's table row documents `Gemini CLI | ~/.gemini/settings.json | User-global | Literal base64`. Task 3.9 edits `skills/langfuse/scripts/install-mcp.sh`, and the wp-skills gate requires that file to contain zero gemini references -- which means the `WRITE_GEMINI` variable (install-mcp.sh:39), the `--no-gemini` and `--claude-only` flags (lines 48-49) and the `~/.gemini/settings.json` writer (lines 155-158) all disappear. The doc will then instruct operators to use flags that no longer exist. This is precisely the human-facing-instruction class D6 says is in scope, not the narrative class it defers.
findings.resolution: Add `docs/cross-repo-setup.md` to task 5.3's file list, to design.md § In-scope user-facing set, and to the wp-docs-finalize gate's file enumeration (work-packages.yaml:357). It is a two-line prose edit plus a table-row deletion.

findings.description: Nit: the `agent-identity` spec delta is the only one of the eight capabilities that no task claims. `grep -n 'agent-identity|seed_profiles' tasks.md work-packages.yaml` returns nothing, and no task's `**Spec scenarios**` line names it, while every other delta is referenced (configuration, agent-archetypes, agent-coordinator, evaluation-framework, coordinator-kanban-viz, codebase-analysis, skill-workflow all appear). The delta introduces a new scenario -- "Retired harness profile survives seeding" -- asserting that `seed_profiles_from_config()` leaves an orphaned `gemini_local` row untouched and raises no error. That is the behavioural contract that makes the applied-migrations carve-out safe, and nothing in the plan writes a test for it. Related: the scenario "Seed creates new profile" pins `grok-local` to `trust_level: 3`, but `contracts/roster.md` declares no per-vendor trust levels and task 2.2 does not enumerate them, so the agents.yaml value is unpinned.
findings.resolution: Add a task under Phase 2 (wp-coordinator owns `agent-coordinator/tests/`) writing a `seed_profiles_from_config()` test for the retired-profile scenario, tag it `**Spec scenarios**: agent-identity.1`, and pin the new vendors' `trust_level` values in `contracts/roster.md` § Canonical strings so 2.2 has a source of truth.

findings.description: Nit: two copies of the provider-model-map schema now exist and have already diverged, reintroducing the pattern D8 removed. `contracts/provider-model-map.schema.json` is still listed in `work-packages.yaml:16` under `contracts.openapi.files`, while design.md § Merge-order coupling states the schema's runtime home is `openspec/schemas/provider-model-map.schema.json` and `test_contracts.py:12-14` carries an explicit comment forbidding change-directory resolution. `diff` shows they differ in `$id`, `description`, the `providers` constraints (the change-dir copy already has `propertyNames.enum` + `required`, the promoted one still has `minProperties: 1`), and an `examples` block containing placeholder strings like `"<resolved by task 1.1>"`. Nothing validates the change-dir copy, so it is a spec-shaped artifact with no consumer that will archive alongside the change.
findings.resolution: Delete `contracts/provider-model-map.schema.json` and remove it from `work-packages.yaml:16`, keeping the desired v2 provider-key closure as prose in `contracts/roster.md` (which task 3.6 already cites), so `openspec/schemas/` remains the single home.

findings.description: Nit: wp-frontend's gate hardcodes a derived count -- `test "$(git grep -lIi gemini -- apps/kanban-viz | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "3"` -- which is the numeric-gate class D8.1 explicitly removed ("Gates are existing test suites plus inline one-line git grep checks -- no derived numbers"). The number is correct today (the tree currently lists 4 files: VendorSwimlanes.test.tsx plus the three provenance files, dropping to 3 after task 4.1), but any unrelated in-flight change that adds or removes a mention turns this red for reasons unrelated to the roster. Separately, tasks.md:246 writes the component-untouched assertion as `git diff --quiet main -- ...` while work-packages.yaml:278 writes `git diff --quiet main... -- ...`; the three-dot form (merge-base) is the correct one for a package branch, and the two artifacts should not disagree.
findings.resolution: Replace the count with a set assertion naming the three carve-out files, e.g. `test "$(git grep -lIi gemini -- apps/kanban-viz ':!src/hooks/useCoordinator.ts' ':!src/__tests__/useCoordinator.test.tsx' ':!src/lib/coordinator-types.ts')" = ""`, and make tasks.md:246 use `main...` to match.

findings.description: Optional: task 3.11 removes `google-generativeai>=0.8.6` (skills/pyproject.toml:22, in the `sdk` optional-dependencies extra) but leaves the `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` pin `httplib2>=0.32.0` whose own comment justifies it as "Brought in transitively via google-api-python-client / google-auth-httplib2 (pulled by the sdk extra)". Once the google chain is gone the override has no remaining justification and its comment becomes false. Harmless at runtime; it is a stale-rationale hazard for the next person auditing overrides.
findings.resolution: After `uv lock` in task 3.11, check whether httplib2 still appears in `skills/uv.lock`; if it does not, drop the override block and its comment. Same check for `agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml` in task 2.9.

findings.description: Optional: task 1.2's contingency -- "**On failure of E2**: apply Approach B (thin wrapper) narrowly to grok" -- has no corresponding task and no writable location. wp-empirical's `write_allow` is `design.md` alone (work-packages.yaml:54-55), so it can record the decision but not create `grok_wrapper.sh`; no Phase 2 task mentions a wrapper either, and the wp-coordinator gate would then require a new script that appears in no task's file list. The E6 contingency is handled better ("re-scope task 2.6 before starting it" names a concrete task). Low probability, but if E2 is refuted the plan stalls on a decision nobody owns.
findings.resolution: Add one sentence to task 2.2: "If E2 was refuted, additionally create `agent-coordinator/scripts/grok_wrapper.sh` and point `grok-local`'s `cli.command` at it." That places the fallback inside wp-coordinator's existing write scope.

findings.description: The scope inventory is complete and bidirectionally verified -- this is the plan's strongest property and worth preserving through any rework. Running design.md's own authoritative command against each package's gate scope, every file maps to exactly one task, with no orphans in either direction: 19 files under `agent-coordinator` (Makefile->2.8, agents.yaml->2.2, archetypes.yaml+agents_config.py->2.3, five evaluation/ files->2.6, gemini_wrapper.sh->2.8, seed_kanban_board.py+saved-view.json+test_kanban_viz_endpoints.py->2.7, setup_cloud.py+coordination_api.py+test_differential_policy.py+test_feedback.py->2.4, two test_agents_config files->2.1); 45 files under `skills scripts packages` all covered by 3.1-3.11 and 4.2; 4 files under `apps/kanban-viz` (one edited by 4.1, three carve-outs); and all 10 in-scope SKILL.md files confirmed to currently contain gemini. Three other checks also pass on this branch: `openspec validate --all --strict` -> 53 passed / 0 failed; `uv run --project packages/agent-scenarios pytest packages/agent-scenarios/tests -q` -> 36 passed, 1 skipped (D7's agent-scenarios repair works exactly as written, including the round-2 catch about `--project` not changing cwd); and `make -n -C agent-coordinator mcp-setup hooks-setup` -> exit 0. Task 0.1's diagnosis also reproduces precisely (`skills/tests` -> `Interrupted: 1 error during collection`, `No module named 'fastapi'`), and its insistence on pyproject.toml over a venv-only install is correct -- `worktree-bootstrap.sh:47` runs `uv sync --all-extras`, which would discard a direct install.
findings.resolution: No action. Keep the `git grep -lI` inventory command and the per-package gate scopes as the canonical mapping when addressing findings 1-5.
